name: The Nabataean Pantheon
dom: pantheon; Nabataean state religion; caravan trade; sacred kingship
note: Collective grouping the deities worshipped across the Nabataean kingdom from Petra and Bostra to Hegra (Madaʾin Salih), attested in Nabataean Aramaic inscriptions and rock-cut sanctuaries.

name: Shai al-Qaum
dom: protection; caravans; warriors; abstinence from wine
note: Caravan-protector and warrior god 'who drinks no wine and builds no tomb,' named in a bilingual Nabataean altar from Palmyra (CIS II 3978).

name: Aʿra
note: Tutelary god of Bostra closely associated with Dushara, who is titled 'the god of our lord who is in Bostra' in Nabataean Hawran inscriptions.

name: al-Kutbaʾ
note: Scribal and commerce deity (Nabataean counterpart of Babylonian Nabu / Greek Hermes), attested at Petra, Hegra and Sinai; sometimes the goddess al-Kutbay.

name: Manotu
note: Hegran cult-form of the fate-goddess Manat, invoked as 'Manotu and her Qaisha' in the tomb-curse inscriptions of Hegra to protect burials.

name: al-ʿUzza of Petra
note: Petraean cult-form of al-ʿUzza, chief Nabataean goddess identified with Aphrodite, associated with Petra's Temple of the Winged Lions.

name: The Idols of the Kaʿba and the Arabian Sanctuaries
dom: idol cult; tribal patron deities; Arabian sanctuaries
note: Collective of the betyls and idols of the Hijaz and wider Arabia catalogued in Ibn al-Kalbi's Kitab al-Asnam and reflected in Qurʾan 71:23.

name: Isāf
note: Idol at the Kaʿba; in tradition a man petrified for sacrilege, paired with Nāʾila, attested in Ibn al-Kalbi at al-Safa/al-Marwa.

name: Nāʾila
note: Female idol at the Kaʿba, paired with Isāf as a petrified couple, attested in Ibn al-Kalbi at al-Safa/al-Marwa.

name: Manāf
note: Meccan deity whose name survives in the Quraysh name ʿAbd Manaf; listed among the gods of Mecca in Ibn al-Kalbi.

name: Dhu'l-Khalasa
note: White quartz betyl and oracular sanctuary at Tabala in Yemen, 'the Yemeni Kaʿba,' venerated by Daws, Khathʿam and Bajila per Ibn al-Kalbi.

name: Ruda
note: North Arabian astral deity (Venus) attested in Thamudic and Safaitic inscriptions and named in Assyrian records as 'Ruldaiu'; also in Ibn al-Kalbi.

name: Nuhm
note: Deity of the Muzayna tribe whose name survives in the theophoric ʿAbd Nuhm; listed in Ibn al-Kalbi.

name: al-Fals
note: Idol of the Tayyiʾ tribe, a reddish rock outcrop on Jabal Aja serving as a place of asylum, described in Ibn al-Kalbi.

name: Saʿd
note: A tall rock idol of the Banu Milkan (Kinana) on which sacrificial blood was poured, attested in Ibn al-Kalbi.

name: Quzaḥ
note: Storm/rainbow deity associated with the hill Quzaḥ at Muzdalifa near Mecca; Arabic qaws Quzaḥ ('Quzaḥ's bow' = rainbow) preserves his name.

name: Suwāʿ
note: One of the five antediluvian idols of Qurʾan 71:23; later the idol of the Hudhayl tribe at Ruhat per Ibn al-Kalbi.

name: Yaʿūq
note: One of the five antediluvian idols of Qurʾan 71:23 ('the preventer/protector'); horse-formed idol of Hamdan at Khaywan in Yemen per Ibn al-Kalbi.

name: Wadd
note: National god of the Minaean (Maʿin) kingdom and a moon-deity; the formula 'Wd ʾb' (Wadd is father) is widely attested on amulets and inscriptions; one of the five idols of Qurʾan 71:23.

name: Anbay
note: Qatabanian oracular and law-giving god, paired with Ḥawkam; 'Anbay and Ḥawkam' issue decrees in Qatabanian legal inscriptions.

name: Sayin
note: National god of the kingdom of Hadramawt, attested in royal dedications and the great temple at Shabwa; a solar/national patron of Hadramite kingship.

name: Sin (Hawl)
note: Moon-god of Hadramawt bearing the epithet Hawl, attested at Shabwa; distinct from the Mesopotamian Sin though sharing the lunar name.

name: Taʾlab Riyam
note: Tutelary god of the Sabaean tribe Banu Sumʿay, titled 'Taʾlab Riyam' after his sanctuary on the Riyam massif; many oracle and pilgrimage inscriptions record his cult.

name: Hawbas
note: Sabaean deity closely associated with Almaqah, frequently named alongside him at Awwam/Marib and in Dʿmt-period Ethiopia.

name: Dhāt-Ḥimyam
note: One of the two solar 'Ladies' (Dhat = 'She of') of the Sabaean pantheon, a hypostasis of the sun-goddess; her cult was carried to Dʿmt-period Ethiopia.

name: Dhāt-Baʿdan
note: The second solar 'Lady' of the Sabaean pantheon, paired with Dhat-Himyam; both invoked in temple dedications such as those from the Awwam sanctuary.

name: Dhāt-Ẓahrān
note: A further solar 'Lady' epithet of the South-Arabian sun-goddess attested in dedicatory inscriptions, a localized hypostasis of Shams.

name: Basamum
note: South-Arabian god of healing, his name connected to the balsam/aromatic plant (bsm); attested in votive cure-texts.

name: Nasr
note: A South/West-Arabian deity ('vulture/eagle') named in Qurʾan 71:23 and attested in onomastics; venerated in the Himyaritic/Yemeni sphere.

name: Yagūth
dom: protection; aid in war; lion form
note: Pre-Islamic deity ('he helps') named in Qurʾan 71:23 alongside Yaʿuq and Nasr; lion-idol of Madhhij/Murad in Yemen per Ibn al-Kalbi.

name: The Pre-Christian Aksumite Pantheon
note: The pagan deities worshipped in the Dʿmt kingdom and pre-Christian Aksum, attested in the pre-monotheist inscriptions of King Ezana and in Dʿmt-period South-Arabian-derived dedications.

name: Mahrem
note: Chief god and divine ancestor of the Aksumite kings, 'invincible to the enemy'; Ezana's Greek inscription equates him with Ares and styles the king 'son of Mahrem'.

name: Astar
note: Aksumite reflex of the South-Arabian astral god ʿAthtar (Venus), named first in Ezana's pre-Christian triad 'Astar, Beher and Medr'.

name: Beher
note: Aksumite god of the sea (later 'land/country'), named in Ezana's triad; in the Greek version the maritime deity corresponds to Poseidon.

name: Medr
note: Aksumite earth god (Geʿez medr = 'earth/land'), the third member of Ezana's pre-Christian triad, aligned with the Greek earth deity.

name: Bel of Palmyra
note: Head of the Palmyrene pantheon, worshipped in the great Temple of Bel (dedicated 32 CE); a Bel form assimilated to Babylonian Bel-Marduk, heading the astral triad with Yarhibol and Aglibol.

name: Yarhibol
note: Palmyrene solar god, originally guardian of the sacred spring Efqa, depicted with a radiate nimbus and flanking Bel in the Temple of Bel.

name: Aglibol
note: Palmyrene lunar god depicted with a crescent, paired with Malakbel in the Sacred Garden cult and flanking Bel in the Temple of Bel.

name: Malakbel
note: Palmyrene solar and vegetation god ('Messenger of Bel'), paired with Aglibol; the bilingual altar in Rome equates him with Sol Sanctissimus.

name: Allat of Palmyra
note: Arab goddess worshipped at Palmyra in her own sanctuary, assimilated to armed Athena, attested in Palmyrene and bilingual dedications.

name: Sin of Harran
note: The moon god of the Ehulhul sanctuary at Harran, the principal lunar cult of the Aramean/Assyrian north; named in the Sefire treaty curses and rebuilt by Nabonidus.

name: Rakib-El
note: 'Charioteer of El', tutelary dynastic god of the kings of Samʾal/Zincirli, named in the 8th-c. BCE Hadad, Panamuwa and Kilamuwa inscriptions.

name: Sahar
note: Aramean moon deity (Aramaic shr, 'crescent') invoked among the gods of the royal house at Samʾal in the Panamuwa inscriptions of Zincirli.

name: Kubaba of Carchemish
note: Tutelary goddess of Carchemish, a leading deity of the Syro-Hittite/Aramean north in Luwian and Aramaic inscriptions; later underlies Anatolian Kybele.

name: Elagabal of Emesa
note: The sun god of Emesa ('Ila gabal, god of the mountain') worshipped as a conical black betyl; his priest-emperor Elagabalus installed the stone in Rome, attested on coinage and by Herodian.

name: Azizos
note: The morning-star deity of Edessa, paired with Monimos as the two attendants of the sun; identified with Venus/Phosphoros by Julian (Hymn to King Helios).

name: Monimos
note: The evening-star deity of Edessa (Aramaic mnʿm, 'the favourable one'), twin attendant of the sun alongside Azizos, named by Julian (Hymn to King Helios).

name: The Supreme Triad of Urartu
dom: national pantheon; divine hierarchy; sovereignty; war; storm; sun
note: The organizing triad of the Urartian state pantheon — Khaldi (supreme/war), Teisheba (storm), Shivini (sun) — opening the 79-deity Meher Kapisi god-list of Ishpuini and Minua.

name: Bagmashtu
dom: consort of Khaldi; fertility; regional cult
note: Consort of Khaldi at Musasir (Ardini); where most of Urartu names Arubani as Khaldi's wife, Musasir dedications name 'Khaldi and his wife Bagmashtu', a regional consort tradition.

name: Selardi
note: Urartian moon deity named in the Meher Kapisi god-list; gender and full role debated, attestation limited to the divine list.

name: Tushpuea
dom: consort of Shivini; the city of Tushpa
note: Urartian goddess listed third in the female-deity sequence of the Meher Kapisi inscription (paralleling Shivini); the capital Tushpa is held to derive its name from her.

name: Huba
note: Consort of the storm-god Teisheba in the Urartian god-list, corresponding to Hurrian Hepat, consort of Teshub, consistent with Teisheba being the Urartian reception of Teshub.

name: Sardi
note: Urartian astral/star deity named in the Meher Kapisi god-list, identified by a single domain and a sacrifice allotment with no surviving narrative.

name: The Spear of Khaldi
dom: war; divine victory; royal legitimation; weapon cult
note: The lance of Khaldi was a sacred weapon embodying the war-god's power; the Karagunduz stele praises it as victorious, and Khaldi's temples were 'houses of weapons'.

name: Cosus
dom: war; battle; warrior protection; tribal defence
note: War-god attested by ~20 Latin votive inscriptions in Galicia and northern Portugal, interpreted via interpretatio romana as a Mars-type god of the Callaeci; sometimes identified with Cariociecus.

name: Reue
note: Supreme/sky deity (from IE *dyeu-) in Lusitanian ritual texts including the Cabeço das Fraguas inscription and Arronches plaque, with epithets Reve Anabaraego and Reve Larauco.

name: Runesocesius
note: War/javelin god attested at the São Miguel da Mota / Alentejo cult region, connected to the Endovelicus sanctuary complex.

name: Bormanicus
dom: thermal springs; healing waters; medicinal baths
note: Thermal-spring/healing-waters god attested at the hot-spring sanctuary of Caldas de Vizela; of the Celtic Bormo/Borvo family of spring deities.

name: Tongoenabiagus
note: Spring deity attested at a sacred spring beside the river Cávado at Braga; the -nabiagus element links it to the Nabia water-deity family.

name: Arentius and Arentia
note: A male-female divine pair attested in the Lusitanian region of Egitania and adjacent Extremadura, often invoked with toponymic epithets.

name: Quangeius
note: Local tutelary deity attested by Latin votive inscriptions from the Lusitanian Egitania/Beira region.

name: Vestius Aloniecus
note: Indigenous Callaecian tutelary deity attested at Lourizán (Pontevedra) receiving animal offerings; Aloniecus likely a toponymic epithet.

name: Mistress of the Labyrinth
dom: labyrinth; sanctuary mistress; honey offering; Cretan cult
note: da-pu2-ri-to-jo po-ti-ni-ja ('Mistress of the Labyrinth') receives honey in Linear B tablet KN Gg 702 — the earliest textual attestation of the labyrinth, a distinct Cretan Potnia.

name: Drimios
dom: son of Zeus; minor Pylian deity
note: di-ri-mi-jo on Linear B tablet PY Tn 316, explicitly called di-wo i-je-we ('son of Zeus'); a distinct Mycenaean deity with no surviving Olympian identity.

name: Qe-ra-si-ja
note: qe-ra-si-ja (masc. qe-ra-si-jo) receives offerings on Knossos tablets; read as 'the Theran goddess' or a beast-cult deity, a distinct Cretan-Mycenaean name.

name: Pipituna
note: pi-pi-tu-na, a goddess receiving offerings on Knossos tablets (KN Fp series); a pre-Greek/Minoan-substrate theonym with no Olympian identity.

name: Dopota
note: do-po-ta (probably 'Despotes / the Lord', masculine counterpart to Potnia) receives offerings on Pylos tablets; a distinct titular deity.

name: Trisheros
note: ti-ri-se-ro-e (Tris-heros, 'the Thrice-Hero') receives offerings on PY Tn 316, the earliest attestation of Mycenaean hero/ancestor cult.

name: Iphimedeia
note: i-pi-me-de-ja on PY Tn 316; though later myth knows Iphimedeia as a mortal heroine, in the Pylos tablet she is a divine cult-recipient.

name: Thracian Horseman (Heros)
dom: horseman; hunting; healing; tomb/heroic protection; chthonic
note: The most widespread Thracian divine figure, attested by hundreds of votive and funerary rider-reliefs across Thrace and Moesia, associated with hunting, healing and heroic/chthonic protection.

name: Pleistoros
note: War-god of the Thracian Apsinthii recorded by Herodotus (9.119), to whom they sacrificed the Persian Oeobazus.

name: Zibelthiurdos
note: Thracian storm/sky god attested in Greek and Latin inscriptions of the Roman period, equated with Zeus/Jupiter as a thunder deity.

name: Kandaon
note: A Thracian/Macedonian war-god identified with Ares in late Greek sources (Lycophron's Alexandra and scholia); attestation literary rather than epigraphic.

name: Aritene
note: Indigenous Meroitic god named on a faience medallion from the royal cemetery of Meroe (read by Priese as a solar deity) and in the Karanog mortuary inscription (REM 0277).

name: Mash
note: Obscure indigenous Meroitic god named alongside Aritene in the Karanog mortuary inscription of Haramadeye; character otherwise unknown.

name: Napir
dom: moon; night sky; protection of the gods
note: Elamite moon god ('the shining one'), theophoric in Untash-Napirisha; titled 'protector of the gods', invoked in the Neo-Elamite inscription of Hanni of Ayapir (EKI 75) and attested at Susa.

name: Tirutur
note: Elamite god regularly paired with Tepti in Neo-Elamite royal inscriptions; in the Hanni of Ayapir text the kitin of Tepti and Tirutur is invoked with Napir, Simut and Humban.

name: Suhsipa
note: Elamite deity with a temple at Dur-Untash (Tchoga Zanbil) alongside Lagamar and Napirisha; grouped by Henkelman among gods of the husa, a funerary/netherworld sphere.
